newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Hambro Countrywide sees more growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Hambro Countrywide sees more growth.

text.p: UK estate agency and financial products group Hambro Countrywide Plc expects further growth during 1997, its managing director Harry Hill said on Thursday.
Earlier the group announced a significant swing into pre-tax profit of 30.8 million stg for 1996 compared with a loss of 3.9 million stg in 1995.

While delighted by the results, Hill said the firm can do more. "I think we are only half way there yet...if we get to anything like the volumes that we anticipate this year...the prospects are obviously very exciting," Hill told Reuters.

Hill said the impending election in the UK would not slow Hambro Countrywide's business and a victory for the opposition Labour party could in fact benefit the firm's clients, who might feel better off. "I don't think it will make much difference either way," he added. He said Hambro Countrywide, which is 52 percent owned by UK merchant bank Hambros Plc, had sold more mortgages and retail financial services during February than in any other month in its history.

And there was no sign of change to the direct correlation between people buying houses and financial products from the group. "Most people want to do most things if they can, easily and comfortably under one roof," Hill said.
While there are a growing number of competitors in the market-place, Hill said he did not see Hambro Countrywide's margins being pinched as a result.
The group also announced it would break with tradition and move into the London property market, with the acquisition of estate agency and lettings business Faron Sutaria & Co for 7.45 million stg.
"From the middle of this year we will have nine offices under Faron's banner and we would hope in the next two years to have another seven," he said.
Asked if Hambro Countrywide planned to make any further acquisitions, Hill said "We aren't talking to anyone today".

As for Hambro Countrywide's own future, chairman Christopher Sporborg said there was little chance of a change in the current shareholding by Hambros. Hill said the UK housing recovery seemed to be "pretty well across the land" and March had started well, following a 25 percent increase in estate agency sales in January and February of 1997 compared with the previous year.
"It is busier everywhere, there's a good supply of houses coming on the market," Hill said, adding that prices were rising, although more substantially in the south east and especially in London.
He said there was enormous pent-up demand for houses but added that significant price rises in some parts would probably stabilise and prices would find their own levels.
And all the factors were in place for a long, sustained economic recovery in the UK and within that context house prices would increase, Hill added.
Shares in Hambro Countrywide, which also announced a final dividend of 1.5 pence to make a total dividend of 2.0 pence, were down 3.5 pence at 1000 GMT at 124 pence.
